newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: CRICKET-SLOW PITCH FORCES WINDIES TO WORK HARD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SLOW PITCH FORCES WINDIES TO WORK HARD.

text.p: India's bowlers did their best to put West Indies under pressure after a disappointing morning on the fourth day of the second test at Queen's Park Oval on Monday.
The home side were 34 for one in their second innings at tea, still trailing by 106 runs, having earlier taken the last seven Indian wickets for 69 to bowl out their opponents for 436.
India had hoped for a bigger lead on a pitch of increasingly slow, low bounce, but seamer Abey Kuruvilla struck an early blow in West Indies' second innings when he removed Sherwin Campbell for four.
Opener Campbell was adjudged lbw to a ball which cut back into him with the score on 25, offering proof that batting is unlikely to be easy for West Indies in the last four sessions of the match.
They could do with someone showing similar resolve to opener Navjot Sidhu who batted for over 11 hours to became only the third Indian batsman to take a double-hundred off West Indies.
He was finally bowled by Curtly Ambrose for 201, including 19 fours and a six.
Ambrose also bowled Mohammed Azharuddin and finished with figures of five for 87, stealing the limelight from newcomer Mervyn Dillon who took three for 92 in his first test.
